sections.h2: Which Owen County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in Owenton matter here: one collects the money, one decides the value, and one keeps records once a bill goes unpaid or an appeal is filed.

Owen County offices involved in property tax (Owen County government pages)
OfficeJobContact
SheriffTakes in state, county and school district tax103 W. Perry St.; 502-484-3363; Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-4 p.m.
Property Valuation AdministrationSets values and fields bill questions502-484-5172
County ClerkDelinquent tax listings, deeds, liens136 W. Bryan St.; 502-484-2213; Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m., lunch closure noon to 1

On its own page the sheriff stresses that the office assigns no values, so a dispute over the amount begins with the PVA.

sections.h2: What is Owen County's size and history?
sections.html:
About 354 square miles of northern Kentucky belong to Owen County, with only 3.1 square miles of that under water. Owenton is the seat, Glencoe and Gratz are the lone other cities, and Carroll, Gallatin, Grant, Scott, Franklin and Henry counties surround it. Density is thin, at 32.1 residents per square mile in 2020.

Approved on February 6, 1819, the county took land from Franklin, Scott, Gallatin and Pendleton counties and honors Abraham Owen, a legislator killed at Tippecanoe. Hesler was the first seat, and in 1822 the court moved to the new town of Owenton. Settlers found numerous Native American burial mounds. Once locks and dams went onto the Kentucky River, regular packet boats between Frankfort and Louisville began stopping at Gratz and Monterey in 1844. The county is dry apart from a winery and limited sales inside Owenton.

sections.h2: How many people live in Owen County, and what do they pay for housing?
sections.html:
Owen County once held far more people than it does now, as the decennial census table on Wikipedia shows.

  • 2,031 people in 1820, climbing to a high of 17,676 in 1890.
  • A slide to 7,470 by 1970, the low point.
  • 10,547 in 2000, 11,278 in 2020 and an estimated 11,601 in mid-2025.

Recent survey figures point to an owner-dominated market with long drives to work.

  • Homes owned by their occupants carry a median value of $168,700, and 88.0 percent of the 4,252 households fall in that group.
  • Mortgage holders spend $1,385 a month at the median, and renters pay $830.
  • The typical household earns $61,134, and 13.9 percent of residents live in poverty.
  • Getting to work takes 41.9 minutes on average, the longest figure in the four-county Census table.
  • Only 17 building permits were issued in 2025.

The 2020 census adds that all of Owen County's residents lived in rural areas. Of 5,323 housing units, 18.3 percent stood vacant, a high share that includes seasonal and unsold property. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.2 percent and the rental rate 6.3 percent. Median age was 41.9, and about 26.0 percent of households were one person living alone. Residents 65 or older made up 18.3 percent of that population, and children under 18 made up 24.3 percent.

Other Census measures round out the profile. Per capita income is $30,369, households average 2.64 people, and owners without a mortgage pay a median $434 a month. High school graduates are 86.5 percent of adults, 13.1 percent of people under 65 report a disability, and 3.2 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home. The county seat's own tax and occupancy rules can differ from the county's, so a house inside Owenton, Glencoe or Gratz deserves a question to city hall as well.

sections.h2: What are the payment dates for an Owen County bill?
sections.html:
Sheriffs across Kentucky use the schedule in KRS 134.015. Owen County residents get a 2 percent break for paying by November 1, owe the stated amount until year end, and add 5 percent in January, then 10 percent from February.

April 15 ends the sheriff's collection season. What remains unpaid turns into a certificate of delinquency at the County Clerk, with a lien noted against the parcel.

sections.h2: How do Owen County owners contest a valuation?
sections.html:
A PVA appeal guide advises opening with a talk at the PVA office. Arrive with your own value figure and proof, such as nearby sales, an appraisal, damage photos or contractor quotes. Landlords add rent and expense records.

  1. Talk to the PVA while the roll is open for inspection each spring.
  2. Collect the appeal form from the clerk at 136 W. Bryan Street and return it by the next business day after inspection ends.
  3. Present your evidence to a local board of three residents.
  4. If the ruling stands and you disagree, send the state Board of Tax Appeals a letter within a month of the notice.

You may pay on your own claimed value while an appeal is pending, but a higher final figure produces a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent Owen County bills?
sections.html:
The clerk's website posts the delinquent list along with investor registration forms. The revenue department places a normal-schedule sale between July 14 and August 28, no sooner than 90 days after the bills reach the clerk.

  • Each month adds 1 percent interest.
  • The county attorney sends two letters, and the second names the sale date.
  • Newspaper notices run roughly a month to six weeks before the sale.
  • A certificate that sells to an investor can carry added fees.

If you are selling a listed parcel, ask the clerk (502-484-2213) for a written payoff.

sections.h2: Which breaks apply to Owen County property?
sections.html:
Homeowners who are 65 or older or totally disabled can shelter part of a home's assessed value through the homestead exemption. The amount is set by the state and reviewed every two years. A veteran with a total service-connected disability applies once, but a buyer starts fresh.

Working farm acreage is assessed at agricultural value, not market value, which can cut the taxable amount sharply. Before a farm is sold or split, ask the PVA whether the tract qualifies.

sections.h2: What charges follow an Owen County sale to the closing table?
sections.html:
The transfer tax is the seller's: half a dollar per $500 of value, with any partial block counted whole (KRS 142.050). Sold at the $168,700 median, a house spans 338 units and costs $169.00. The clerk wants proof of payment before taking the deed.

The deed itself must list the full price, both mailing addresses and a forwarding address for the next tax bill (KRS 382.135), or the clerk cannot file it.

sections.h2: Which economic facts matter to Owen County buyers and sellers?
sections.html:
Local spending is modest. Shops in the county sold $83.9 million of goods in 2022, about $7,426 for each resident, while health care and social assistance took in $24.6 million and lodging and restaurants $7.0 million. In 2023 the county had 133 employers, 969 jobs and a $39.9 million payroll, and employment slipped 1.5 percent from 2022. A further 764 nonemployer businesses were operating in 2024.

A bachelor's degree is held by 18.3 percent of adults, and 9.0 percent of people under 65 have no health coverage. About 90.4 percent of residents stayed in one house for a full year. Broadband reaches 80.4 percent of households, 89.3 percent have a computer, and 598 residents are veterans. Labor force participation is 58.0 percent.

faqs.q: Which office decides what my Owen County property is worth?
faqs.a: The Property Valuation Administration, 502-484-5172. Collection is the sheriff's job, valuation is not.

faqs.q: Where is the Owen County tax office?
faqs.a: In the sheriff's office at 103 W. Perry St., Owenton (502-484-3363), Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: What would the state transfer tax cost on a typical Owen County sale?
faqs.a: $169.00 for a $168,700 sale, counting 338 units of $500 at 50 cents each.

faqs.q: What if my bill is still open after April 15?
faqs.a: Phone the County Clerk, 502-484-2213. The bill has become a certificate of delinquency, with a lien and monthly interest of 1 percent.

faqs.q: Is a homestead exemption available in Owen County?
faqs.a: Yes, through the PVA, for residents who are 65 or older or totally disabled. Whoever buys the house applies separately.
